components.note: 大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.
疒 (sickness) shows 疼 relates to pain or discomfort.
冬 (dōng) gives a sound close to téng, sharing a similar consonant sound.

example.hanzi: 他昨晚没睡好,今天头疼。
example.pinyin: tā zuówǎn méi shuìhǎo, jīntiān tóuténg.
example.english: He didn't sleep well last night, so today he has a headache.
example.fact: Willow bark, rich in a compound called salicin, was used for pain relief in ancient Egypt and Greece thousands of years before modern medicine existed. In 1897, Bayer chemist Felix Hoffmann synthesized a more stable version of the active compound, giving the world aspirin — still one of the most widely used pain relievers today.

components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun is what disappears as evening falls
免 (to escape, avoid) — pictured as the sun slipping away, giving 晚 its sense of 'late, evening'
宀 (roof) marks the setting — a house or hall.
妟 (a woman 女 beneath the sun 日) suggests ease and comfort — people gathered comfortably under a roof, giving 宴 its meaning 'banquet, feast.'

example.hanzi: 公司为客户举办了一场豪华晚宴。
example.pinyin: gōngsī wèi kèhù jǔbànle yī chǎng háohuá wǎnyàn.
example.english: The company held a lavish banquet for its clients.
example.fact: The Field of the Cloth of Gold in 1520 was a diplomatic summit between England's Henry VIII and France's Francis I, built around weeks of jousting, feasting, and banquets so extravagant that they nearly bankrupted both royal treasuries. Despite the spectacle, the two kings failed to form a lasting alliance and were at war with each other again within a few years.

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 贵 relates to worth and cost.
方 (a flag/banner) — a shared banner under which a group gathers.
矢 (arrow) — warriors bound by oath under one flag gave 族 its meaning 'clan, ethnic group, tribe.'

example.hanzi: 这座城堡曾经属于一位贵族。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò chéngbǎo céngjīng shǔyú yī wèi guìzú.
example.english: This castle once belonged to a nobleman.
example.fact: The Domesday Book, compiled in 1086 on the orders of William the Conqueror, catalogued nearly every landholding in England so the new Norman nobility could be taxed accurately. It remains one of the oldest and most detailed public administrative records in European history, and historians still consult it today.

components.note: 以 traces back to an oracle-bone pictograph of a person bent over holding a farming tool or plow. The image of putting an implement to use gave 以 its core meaning 'to use, by means of,' which later extended to the grammatical sense of 'in order to' or 'according to.'
阝 (a mound/wall) — 防 relates to defensive walls and prevention
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 防 is also pronounced fáng, a close match

万 is the simplified form of 萬, whose ancient pictograph depicted a scorpion with its claws and segmented tail. Because scorpions were imagined appearing in enormous swarms, the character was borrowed to represent the number ten thousand, and the original 'scorpion' sense was later written with an added insect radical, 蠆.
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.

example.hanzi: 出门前带把伞,以防万一下雨。
example.pinyin: chūmén qián dài bǎ sǎn, yǐfángwànyī xiàyǔ.
example.english: Bring an umbrella before going out, just in case it rains.
example.fact: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, carved into a mountainside on a remote Norwegian island, stores duplicate seed samples from gene banks around the world as insurance against war, disease, or climate disaster. Built to withstand earthquakes and rising sea levels, it currently holds well over a million seed samples, all kept just in case.

components.note: 攵 (an action radical) — an older semantic link to opening something up.
尚 (shàng) gives a sound close to chǎng, sharing the same rhyme.
廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'

example.hanzi: 她把窗户敞开,让新鲜空气进来。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ chuānghù chǎngkāi, ràng xīnxiān kōngqì jìnlái.
example.english: She opened the window wide to let in fresh air.
example.fact: Boeing's factory in Everett, Washington is the largest building in the world by volume, and its hangar doors open wide enough to roll out multiple wide-body jets side by side. The facility is so large that employees sometimes use bicycles to get from one end of the factory floor to the other.

components.note: 囗 (an enclosure) surrounds 大 (a person, arms outstretched), originally picturing someone resting on a mat within a room.
That sense of relying on something to rest upon extended metaphorically to 因's modern meaning 'reason, cause' — something an action rests upon.
糸 (thread) — plain, undyed silk thread
龶 — a plant stem, from which the raw silk thread hangs

example.hanzi: 天气是影响农业产量的重要因素。
example.pinyin: tiānqì shì yǐngxiǎng nóngyè chǎnliàng de zhòngyào yīnsù.
example.english: Weather is an important factor affecting agricultural yield.
example.fact: The Rh factor in human blood, the same one behind the '+' or '-' in a blood type, was discovered in 1940 by Karl Landsteiner and Alexander Wiener after they noticed that rabbit antibodies raised against rhesus monkey blood also reacted with most human blood. Identifying this factor was crucial for preventing dangerous immune reactions during blood transfusions and pregnancy.

components.note: 阝 (from 邑, city) — an old tie to a place name, per its 'city' etymology.
有 (yǒu) gives a sound close in initial to yù, though the rhyme has drifted over time.
Heart — feeling gloomy is an emotional state.
Gives the sound mén, related to mèn but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 考试没考好,他心里很郁闷。
example.pinyin: kǎoshì méi kǎohǎo, tā xīnlǐ hěn yùmèn.
example.english: He did poorly on the exam and felt very gloomy.
example.fact: Seasonal Affective Disorder is a form of depression linked to reduced sunlight exposure, and it is markedly more common in far-northern regions like Scandinavia and Alaska during the darkest winter months. Light therapy, using a bright lamp for a set period each morning, is one of the most common treatments recommended by doctors.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/place) — represents a location or settlement.
东 (east) — a settlement facing east gave 陈 meanings like 'to arrange, display,' and it became a common Chinese surname.
辶 (to walk) — narrating something is like walking a listener through events
术 (shù) gives the sound — an exact match with 述's reading shù

example.hanzi: 律师向法官陈述了案件的经过。
example.pinyin: lǜshī xiàng fǎguān chénshùle ànjiàn de jīngguò.
example.english: The lawyer stated the details of the case to the judge.
example.fact: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in 1948, was the first document to formally state a set of fundamental rights believed to belong to all people. It has since been translated into more than 500 languages, making it one of the most translated documents in the world.

components.note: 並 (side by side, together) — represents everyone, all people.
日 (sun) — everyone standing together under the same sun gave 普 its meaning 'universal, general, widespread.'
辶 (to walk, movement) — 通 relates to passing through or getting somewhere.
甬 (yǒng) gives a hint of the sound — 通 is pronounced tōng, a connection that has shifted over time.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 他只是一个普通人,过着平凡的生活。
example.pinyin: tā zhǐshì yī gè pǔtōngrén, guòzhe píngfán de shēnghuó.
example.english: He is just an ordinary person, living an unremarkable life.
example.fact: The Voyager Golden Record, launched into space in 1977, includes images meant to represent ordinary human life on Earth — people eating, working, and raising families — intended for any intelligent life that might one day encounter the spacecraft. Both Voyager probes have since left the solar system and continue traveling through interstellar space.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
足 depicts a leg (the upper shape) above a foot — a simple picture of the human leg and foot, giving 足 its meaning 'foot, to be sufficient.'

example.hanzi: 这份报告的数据明显不足。
example.pinyin: zhè fèn bàogào de shùjù míngxiǎn bùzú.
example.english: The data in this report is clearly insufficient.
example.fact: Scurvy, caused by insufficient vitamin C, devastated sailors on long ocean voyages for centuries, killing more seamen than storms or combat. In 1747, ship's surgeon James Lind ran one of the first controlled clinical trials in history and showed that citrus fruit cured the disease, decades before vitamin C itself was even identified.

components.note: 女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
口 (mouth) — words spoken by a mouth are what reach the ear, giving 听 its meaning 'to listen.'
斤 stands in for the ear in this simplified character — the target that spoken words reach.

example.hanzi: 这首歌的旋律非常好听。
example.pinyin: zhè shǒu gē de xuánlǜ fēicháng hǎotīng.
example.english: The melody of this song is very pleasant to listen to.
example.fact: Humpback whales produce long, complex songs made of repeating phrases that can travel for many kilometers underwater and be picked up by whales far across an ocean basin. Researchers have found that these songs evolve over time and can spread between whale populations almost like a cultural trend.

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — links 边's meaning to a boundary or edge one moves along.
臱 (biān) gives the sound — 边 is also pronounced biān, an exact match.
土 (earth) — 境 relates to land and territory, extended to mean 'environment, boundary'
竟 (jìng) gives the sound — 境 is also pronounced jìng, an exact match

example.hanzi: 士兵们日夜守卫着边境。
example.pinyin: shìbīngmen rìyè shǒuwèizhe biānjìng.
example.english: The soldiers guard the border day and night.
example.fact: The border between the United States and Canada stretches about 8,891 kilometers, including Alaska, making it the longest international border in the world. Much of it is unguarded by fences, relying instead on periodic monitoring and shared agreements between the two countries.

components.note: 发 is the simplified form of 發, whose ancient form combined a bow 弓 with a hand launching an arrow. The image of an arrow shooting forth gave 發 its meaning 'to issue, to send out,' which extended to modern senses like 'to develop' and 'to distribute.'
纟 (thread/silk) — 给 originally related to supplying thread or material, later broadening to mean 'to give.'
合 (hé) gives a hint of the sound — 给 is pronounced gěi, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 老师把成绩单发给了每个学生。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī bǎ chéngjìdān fāgěile měi gè xuésheng.
example.english: The teacher distributed the report cards to every student.
example.fact: Around 1023 CE, the Song dynasty government in China began issuing jiaozi, generally regarded as the world's first government-backed paper currency, after private merchant notes became too widespread to regulate. This innovation predated paper money in Europe by several centuries.

components.note: 疒 depicts a person lying sick in bed, the 'illness' radical.
了 here depicts a resolving action — clearing away an illness gave 疗 its meaning 'to treat, to cure.'
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'

example.hanzi: 医生建议用新的疗法治疗这种疾病。
example.pinyin: yīshēng jiànyì yòng xīn de liáofǎ zhìliáo zhè zhǒng jíbìng.
example.english: The doctor recommended treating this disease with a new therapy.
example.fact: Penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic therapy, was discovered by accident in 1928 when Alexander Fleming noticed that mold contaminating one of his bacterial cultures was killing the surrounding bacteria. It wasn't mass-produced until the 1940s, just in time to treat wounded soldiers during World War II, and it is credited with saving hundreds of millions of lives since.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 掩 describes covering or shutting something with the hand.
奄 (yǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 掩.
巾 (cloth) reflects 饰's original connection to adornment made of cloth or fabric.
饣 (a form of 食, shí) gives a sound close to shì, sharing the initial consonant.

example.hanzi: 他试图掩饰自己的紧张。
example.pinyin: tā shìtú yǎnshì zìjǐ de jǐnzhāng.
example.english: He tried to conceal his nervousness.
example.fact: Cuttlefish can change both the color and the texture of their skin within a fraction of a second, using specialized cells called chromatophores to conceal themselves from predators or mimic their surroundings. Despite being colorblind, they can match complex backgrounds with startling accuracy.

components.note: 疋 — a person walking, shown pausing and looking back uncertainly
矢 (an arrow/cane) — an old man's walking stick, held while hesitating
口 (mouth) — 问 relates to speaking, specifically asking a question.
门 (mén) gives a hint of the sound — 问 is pronounced wèn, related but the tone and vowel have shifted.

example.hanzi: 这个问题至今仍是一个疑问。
example.pinyin: zhège wèntí zhìjīn réng shì yī gè yíwèn.
example.english: This question remains a doubt to this day.
example.fact: The philosopher Karl Popper argued that genuine scientific claims must be falsifiable — capable of being proven wrong through observation or experiment. This principle of built-in doubt became one of the central standards used to distinguish science from pseudoscience throughout the twentieth century.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — blocking something is done with the hand.
当 here contributes to the character's form, describing being raised up at the right moment.
亻 (person) — the one settling somewhere.
主 (host, master) — the idea of a person settled in a place as if hosting it, giving 住 its meaning 'to live, reside, stay.'

example.hanzi: 一棵大树挡住了我们的视线。
example.pinyin: yī kē dà shù dǎngzhùle wǒmen de shìxiàn.
example.english: A big tree blocked our view.
example.fact: Beaver dams can grow large enough to block entire rivers and reshape local ecosystems; the largest known beaver dam, in Alberta, Canada, stretches over 850 meters and is visible in satellite imagery. Beavers build these structures instinctively to create the still water they need for safety and food storage.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 操 relates to controlling or handling something.
喿 (zào) gives a sound distantly related to cāo, having drifted apart over time.
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 别再为这点小事操心了。
example.pinyin: bié zài wèi zhè diǎn xiǎoshì cāoxīn le.
example.english: Don't worry about such a small matter anymore.
example.fact: Chronic worry triggers the adrenal glands to release cortisol, a stress hormone that, in short bursts, sharpens focus but that, over long periods, can suppress immune function and disrupt sleep. Studies on prolonged stress have linked it to slower wound healing and greater susceptibility to common illnesses.

components.note: 纟 (thread/silk) — 维 relates to a connecting thread or fiber, extended to mean 'to maintain, to link'
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound connection to 维's reading wéi
扌 (hand) — represents the act of guarding or defending.
户 (door/household) — protecting one's home gave 护 its meaning 'to protect, guard.'

example.hanzi: 政府有责任维护社会秩序。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ yǒu zérèn wéihù shèhuì zhìxù.
example.english: The government has a responsibility to safeguard social order.
example.fact: The Golden Gate Bridge employs a dedicated crew of ironworkers and painters who continuously maintain its signature orange coat, because salty sea air from the Bay corrodes the steel far faster than in a typical environment. The maintenance cycle never truly ends — by the time one end of the bridge is finished, the other end already needs attention again.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 例 relates to an example or precedent set by a particular case
列 (liè) gives a sound close to 例's reading lì, sharing the same initial consonant and tone
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 老师举了一个简单的例子来解释这个概念。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī jǔle yī gè jiǎndān de lìzi lái jiěshì zhège gàiniàn.
example.english: The teacher gave a simple example to explain the concept.
example.fact: The fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster has served as a classic example organism in genetics for over a century, because it breeds quickly, has a short lifespan, and shares many genes with humans. Research using this simple insect has contributed to at least six Nobel Prizes in Physiology or Medicine.

components.note: 犬 (dog) — 献 originally referred to offering a dog in sacrifice, extended to mean 'to offer, present.'
南 (nán) gives a sound distantly related to xiàn, having drifted apart over time.
纟 (thread/silk) — 给 originally related to supplying thread or material, later broadening to mean 'to give.'
合 (hé) gives a hint of the sound — 给 is pronounced gěi, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 这首歌是献给他母亲的。
example.pinyin: zhè shǒu gē shì xiàngěi tā mǔqīn de.
example.english: This song is dedicated to his mother.
example.fact: The Taj Mahal, one of the most recognized buildings in the world, was commissioned by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan as a mausoleum dedicated to his wife, Mumtaz Mahal, who died during childbirth in 1631. Construction took roughly two decades and reportedly involved thousands of craftsmen and artisans brought in from across the empire.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 终 originally referred to the end of a woven thread, extended to mean 'end, final'
冬 (dōng) gives a loose sound connection to 终's reading zhōng
灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 运动员们终于到达了终点。
example.pinyin: yùndòngyuánmen zhōngyú dàodále zhōngdiǎn.
example.english: The athletes finally reached the finish line.
example.fact: The modern marathon's standard distance, 42.195 kilometers, was fixed based on the course used at the 1908 London Olympics, which ran from Windsor Castle to White City Stadium. Earlier Olympic marathons had varied in length, and this particular route just happened to become the permanent standard adopted worldwide.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 做 relates to a person carrying out an action.
故 (cause, reason, to happen) — combined with 亻 (person), 做 came to mean 'to make' or 'to do,' someone actively causing something to happen.

成's ancient form is built from 戊, a pictograph of a bladed halberd, with an added stroke marking a completed strike. The image of a battle brought to a decisive close gave 成 its meaning 'to complete, to accomplish, to become.'

example.hanzi: 她把这块布做成了一条裙子。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ zhè kuài bù zuòchéngle yī tiáo qúnzi.
example.english: She made this piece of cloth into a skirt.
example.fact: Ordinary glass is made by heating common sand, primarily silica, to temperatures above 1,700 degrees Celsius until it melts into a liquid that can be shaped and cooled into a solid, transparent material. Ancient Mesopotamian and Egyptian artisans were making glass objects as early as 3,500 years ago, long before industrial furnaces existed.

components.note: 条 is the simplified form of 條, which paired 木 (tree) with 攸 to describe a slender, flexible branch or twig.
That image of something long and thin let 條 develop into a measure word for narrow strips, streets, and other elongated objects, as well as the noun for a 'note' or 'slip.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 他在桌上留了一张条子。
example.pinyin: tā zài zhuō shàng liúle yī zhāng tiáozi.
example.english: He left a note on the table.
example.fact: The Rosetta Stone, discovered in 1799, carries the same royal decree written in three different scripts — hieroglyphic, Demotic, and Ancient Greek. Because the Greek text could already be read, scholars used the stone to finally decipher Egyptian hieroglyphics, unlocking centuries of previously unreadable inscriptions.

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 纳 originally related to sewing thread into cloth, later extended to 'taking in, accepting'
内 (nèi) gives a sound close to 纳's reading nà, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
Rice/grain — relates to something refined, like husked grain.
Gives the sound zú, related to cuì but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了二战期间纳粹的暴行。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshùle èrzhàn qījiān Nàcuì de bàoxíng.
example.english: This film tells of the Nazis' atrocities during World War II.
example.fact: The Nuremberg Trials, held from 1945 to 1946, were the first international tribunals to prosecute individuals for crimes against humanity, establishing the legal precedent that following orders is not a defense for atrocities. The trials introduced legal concepts still used in international courts today, including genocide as a distinct, prosecutable crime.

meanings: Asia (abbr. for 亞細亞洲|亚细亚洲[Ya4 xi4 ya4 Zhou1])

components.note: A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'
氵 (water) — the water surrounding the land
州 (a stretch of land) — depicted as islands of land within a river

example.hanzi: 中国是亚洲最大的国家之一。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó shì Yàzhōu zuìdà de guójiā zhī yī.
example.english: China is one of the largest countries in Asia.
example.fact: Asia is Earth's largest continent by both area and population, covering roughly 30 percent of the planet's total land area and home to more than 4.7 billion people. It contains both the highest point on Earth, Mount Everest, and the lowest exposed land point, the shore of the Dead Sea.

components.note: 尸 (a body) — 屠 relates to slaughtering, dealing with bodies of animals.
者 (zhě) gives a sound distantly related to 屠's reading tú, having drifted apart over time.
乂 depicts crossed strokes suggesting a cutting action.
木 (wood) here represents a wooden stake — giving 杀 its meaning 'to kill.'

example.hanzi: 历史书记录了那场可怕的屠杀。
example.pinyin: lìshǐshū jìlùle nà chǎng kěpà de túshā.
example.english: The history book records that terrible massacre.
example.fact: The passenger pigeon was once the most abundant bird in North America, with flocks so vast they could darken the sky for hours as they passed overhead. Relentless commercial hunting through the 1800s drove the species from billions of individuals to complete extinction by 1914, one of the fastest documented collapses of an animal population in history.

meanings: strike (i.e. angle of inclination in geology)

components.note: 土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.

向 originally pictured a building (宀) above a mouth-like opening (口), representing a window or doorway of a house facing outward. The idea of an opening 'facing' a particular way gave 向 its meaning 'direction, toward.'

example.hanzi: 专家们讨论了经济未来的走向。
example.pinyin: zhuānjiāmen tǎolùnle jīngjì wèilái de zǒuxiàng.
example.english: Experts discussed the future trend of the economy.
example.fact: In geology, 'strike' describes the compass direction along which a tilted rock layer intersects a horizontal plane, a measurement geologists use to map underground formations and fault lines. Understanding the strike and dip of rock layers along California's San Andreas Fault has been essential to predicting earthquake risk in the region.

components.note: 里 (village, a unit of land) — 野 describes open country beyond the village.
予 (yǔ) reflects an older phonetic link, though the modern readings yě and yǔ have since diverged.
亦 (also, similarly) contributes to the character's form.
虫 (insect) sits below it — an old, dismissive way of grouping outsiders with lowly creatures, behind 蛮's meaning 'barbarian.'

example.hanzi: 这种野蛮的行为让人无法接受。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng yěmán de xíngwéi ràng rén wúfǎ jiēshòu.
example.english: This kind of barbarous behavior is unacceptable.
example.fact: Primatologist Jane Goodall was the first researcher to document chimpanzees engaging in coordinated, sustained violence between rival troops, a finding that startled scientists who had assumed only humans waged organized conflict. Her observations at Gombe Stream National Park in Tanzania in the 1970s reshaped how biologists think about the origins of group aggression.

components.note: 人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
讠 (speech) — relates to 议's meaning 'to discuss, deliberate; opinion.'
义 (yì) gives the sound — 议 is also pronounced yì, an exact match.
宀 (roof) — 室 refers to an enclosed room under a roof
至 (zhì) gives the sound — an exact match with 室's reading shì

example.hanzi: 我们在会议室里讨论了新方案。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zài huìyìshì lǐ tǎolùnle xīn fāng'àn.
example.english: We discussed the new plan in the meeting room.
example.fact: The United Nations Security Council Chamber in New York features a large mural donated by Norway depicting a phoenix rising from ashes, symbolizing a world rebuilding itself after the devastation of World War II. The room has hosted the council's meetings since the UN headquarters opened in 1952.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.
夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'

example.hanzi: 她被提名为最佳女演员。
example.pinyin: tā bèi tímíng wéi zuìjiā nǚ yǎnyuán.
example.english: She was nominated for best actress.
example.fact: Nobel Prize nominations are kept confidential for 50 years before being released to the public in the Nobel archive, meaning nominees and nominators from the mid-twentieth century are only now becoming fully known. Some of the disclosed archives have revealed surprising near-misses, including scientists later found to have been nominated many times without ever winning.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 调's meaning 'to adjust, transfer,' something coordinated through spoken negotiation.
周 (zhōu) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from diào.
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢和陌生人调情。
example.pinyin: tā xǐhuan hé mòshēngrén tiáoqíng.
example.english: He likes to flirt with strangers.
example.fact: Peacocks display their iridescent tail feathers in elaborate courtship dances, and the number and symmetry of eyespots directly influence which males females choose to mate with. Charles Darwin used this kind of showy, seemingly impractical display as a key example when developing his theory of sexual selection.

components.note: 艹 (plant) reflects 董's original meaning related to a type of plant, later used for "to direct, supervise" and as a surname.
重 (zhòng) gives a sound distantly related to dǒng, having drifted apart over time.

事 depicts a hand grasping a forked instrument once used by scribes and officials to record and manage affairs of state, an origin it shares with 史 (scribe) and 吏 (official). That association with the business of governing gave 事 its broad modern meaning 'matter, affair, to work at.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 董事会将在下周开会讨论预算。
example.pinyin: dǒngshìhuì jiāng zài xià zhōu kāihuì tǎolùn yùsuàn.
example.english: The board of directors will meet next week to discuss the budget.
example.fact: The Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602, is widely considered the first corporation to be run by a formal board of directors and to issue shares that could be freely traded on an open exchange. Its structure laid much of the groundwork for how modern publicly traded companies are organized.

components.note: 身 (body) shows 躲 relates to an action of the body, like hiding.
朵 (duǒ) gives the exact sound of 躲.
辶 (to walk) — 避 means to avoid, moving away from something.
辟 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match with 避.

example.hanzi: 小动物们躲避着凶猛的老鹰。
example.pinyin: xiǎo dòngwùmen duǒbìzhe xiōngměng de lǎoyīng.
example.english: The little animals evaded the fierce eagle.
example.fact: The octopus can instantly change both the color and the texture of its skin to evade predators, using muscle-controlled papillae to mimic rocks, coral, or sand within moments. Neuroscientists still don't fully understand how the octopus's decentralized nervous system coordinates such precise camouflage across its entire body.

components.note: 屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
匕 (a kneeling person) — a mourner bowed down in grief.
歹 (skeletal remains) — the corpse being mourned, the source of 死's meaning 'to die, dead.'

example.hanzi: 医生在手术室里面对生死的考验。
example.pinyin: yīshēng zài shǒushùshì lǐ miànduì shēngsǐ de kǎoyàn.
example.english: The doctor faced a test of life or death in the operating room.
example.fact: Telomeres, the protective caps at the ends of chromosomes, shorten slightly every time a cell divides, and once they grow too short, the cell can no longer replicate. This process is closely linked to aging, and the scientists who discovered how telomeres are maintained by the enzyme telomerase won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2009.

components.note: 口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.
禾 (a grain plant) — a sweet-smelling crop
日 — here standing in for sweetness (originally 甘), giving the sense of a pleasant smell
Rice/grain — sugar was traditionally made from grains or cane.
Gives the sound táng, matching the character's reading.

example.hanzi: 他嚼着口香糖走进教室。
example.pinyin: tā jiáozhe kǒuxiāngtáng zǒujìn jiàoshì.
example.english: He walked into the classroom chewing gum.
example.fact: Modern chewing gum traces back to chicle, a natural latex harvested from the sapodilla tree in Central America, which businessman Thomas Adams tried and failed to turn into a rubber substitute in the 1870s. Unable to make it work as rubber, he added flavoring and sold it as gum instead, launching a global industry almost by accident.

components.note: 人 (person), doubled — one person shown following another depicts the idea of accompanying or coming from somewhere.

前's older form combined 止 (a foot) above 舟 (a boat), picturing a foot stepping onto a boat to move forward. That sense of advancing gave 前 its meaning 'front, ahead, before,' while the boat element was eventually replaced by 刀 in the modern simplified shape.

example.hanzi: 从前有一个小村庄。
example.pinyin: cóngqián yǒu yī gè xiǎo cūnzhuāng.
example.english: Once upon a time there was a small village.
example.fact: Homer's epic poems, the Iliad and the Odyssey, are believed to have circulated orally for generations, passed down by professional bards who memorized and improvised the verses, before being written down around the 8th century BCE. This oral tradition relied on repeated formulas and rhythmic patterns that made such enormous poems possible to memorize.

components.note: A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'
火 is the semantic element, tying the character's meaning to fire.
巨 (jù) is read identically to this character, "jù" — a clean phonetic match.

example.hanzi: 运动员高举着火炬跑进体育场。
example.pinyin: yùndòngyuán gāojǔzhe huǒjù pǎojìn tǐyùchǎng.
example.english: The athlete ran into the stadium holding the torch high.
example.fact: The modern Olympic torch relay was introduced at the 1936 Berlin Games, and since then the flame has been carried across oceans by ship, flown by plane, and even carried underwater near Australia's Great Barrier Reef during the 2000 Sydney torch relay. The flame itself is still lit using a parabolic mirror to focus sunlight at Olympia, Greece, exactly as the ancient Greeks did.

components.note: 厂 (a cliff shape) reflects 厌's original meaning related to a rock formation, later shifted to mean "to dislike."
犬 (quǎn) gives a sound distantly related to yàn, having drifted apart over time.
心 (heart) — 恶 relates to an evil or malicious state of heart/mind
亚 (yà) gives a sound distantly related to 恶's reading è, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 她对谎言感到十分厌恶。
example.pinyin: tā duì huǎngyán gǎndào shífēn yànwù.
example.english: She feels great disgust toward lies.
example.fact: Psychologists classify disgust as one of a small set of universal human emotions, recognizable by the same facial expression across virtually every culture studied. Researchers believe it evolved primarily as a defense mechanism to help early humans avoid spoiled food, disease, and other biological contaminants.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — the living thing in bloom.
化 (transformation) — the plant changing into blossom, the source of 花's meaning 'flower.'
木 (tree/wood) — 样 originally referred to a kind of tree, later broadening to mean 'kind, appearance, way.'
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — 样 is pronounced yàng, matching aside from tone.

example.hanzi: 这条围巾有很多漂亮的花样。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo wéijīn yǒu hěn duō piàoliang de huāyàng.
example.english: This scarf has many beautiful patterns.
example.fact: The Fibonacci sequence appears repeatedly in nature's patterns, from the spiral arrangement of seeds in a sunflower head to the scales of a pinecone, because it produces one of the most space-efficient ways to pack growing elements. Botanists call this spiral arrangement phyllotaxis, and it shows up across an enormous range of unrelated plant species.

components.note: 田 (a field) pairs with an element derived from 卯, whose older form suggested something held in place or detained.
Applied to a field, the combination came to mean 'to stay, to remain, to keep,' as in produce left standing rather than harvested.
心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.

example.hanzi: 请留意脚下的台阶。
example.pinyin: qǐng liúyì jiǎoxià de táijiē.
example.english: Please pay attention to the step underfoot.
example.fact: Meerkats take turns acting as sentries, standing upright on their hind legs atop a mound while the rest of the group forages, ready to bark an alarm call the instant a predator like a hawk or jackal appears. Different alarm calls signal different types of threats, and other meerkats react instantly based on which specific call they hear.

components.note: 宀 (roof/house) — relates to 完's meaning 'complete, finish,' as in a fully built house.
元 (yuán) was the phonetic base; the pronunciation later shifted to wán, so only a partial rhyme remains today.

事 depicts a hand grasping a forked instrument once used by scribes and officials to record and manage affairs of state, an origin it shares with 史 (scribe) and 吏 (official). That association with the business of governing gave 事 its broad modern meaning 'matter, affair, to work at.'

example.hanzi: 这件事很快就能完事。
example.pinyin: zhè jiàn shì hěn kuài jiù néng wánshì.
example.english: This matter can be finished very quickly.
example.fact: Barcelona's Sagrada Família basilica has been under continuous construction since 1882, funded largely by private donations and ticket sales rather than government money, with completion now projected around 2026 — well over 140 years after ground was first broken. Architect Antoni Gaudí knew he would never see it finished in his lifetime and reportedly said that was fine, since 'my client is not in a hurry.'

components.note: 扌 (hand) — the hand doing the sowing.
番 (a field marked out into plots) — seeds scattered by hand across it, giving 播 its meaning 'to sow, to spread, to broadcast.'
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 这部电视剧将在周五晚上播出。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànshìjù jiāng zài zhōuwǔ wǎnshàng bōchū.
example.english: This TV drama will be broadcast on Friday evening.
example.fact: Pittsburgh radio station KDKA's broadcast of the 1920 U.S. presidential election results is widely cited as the first regularly scheduled commercial radio broadcast in American history. The station had only just received its official license days earlier, and its early success helped spark a nationwide radio boom within just a few years.

meanings: one's own (child) (i.e. one's child by birth)

components.note: 木 (tree) — traditionally read as a tree that has borne fruit.
立 (standing) — standing close by to watch it grow, evoking closeness and nurture, extended to 亲's meaning 'close, dear; parent, relative.'
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.

example.hanzi: 她终于找到了自己的亲生父母。
example.pinyin: tā zhōngyú zhǎodàole zìjǐ de qīnshēng fùmǔ.
example.english: She finally found her biological parents.
example.fact: Identical twins share nearly all of their DNA, yet they still have different fingerprints, because fingerprint ridges are shaped not just by genes but by random pressures and fluid movements inside the womb during early development. This is why fingerprints remain one of the most reliable ways to distinguish between even genetically identical individuals.

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 运's meaning 'to move, transport,' and by extension 'fortune,' the movement of one's life.
云 (yún) gives a sound hint — 运 is pronounced yùn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
用 is thought to be a pictograph of a wooden pail or bucket used for carrying water — an everyday tool whose practical purpose gave the character its meaning 'to use, to employ.'

example.hanzi: 他善于运用所学的知识解决问题。
example.pinyin: tā shànyú yùnyòng suǒxué de zhīshì jiějué wèntí.
example.english: He is skilled at applying what he has learned to solve problems.
example.fact: The application of Bernoulli's principle, which describes how a fluid's pressure drops as its speed increases, underlies how an airplane's curved wing generates the lift needed to fly. Daniel Bernoulli formulated the mathematical basis for this relationship in 1738, more than a century and a half before the Wright brothers' first flight.

components.note: 大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'
直 (straight, upright) — 真 relates to something level and true.
几 (a small table) — an object placed level and true on a table gave 真 its meaning 'real' or 'true.'

example.hanzi: 孩子的天真笑容让人感到温暖。
example.pinyin: háizi de tiānzhēn xiàoróng ràng rén gǎndào wēnnuǎn.
example.english: The child's innocent smile makes people feel warm.
example.fact: On the Galápagos Islands, many native animals evolved for millennia with no natural land predators, which is why finches and iguanas there famously showed little fear when Charles Darwin and other early visitors first arrived. That naive lack of caution, largely absent in animals from predator-rich mainland habitats, was one of the features that first caught Darwin's attention.

components.note: Person — describes someone falling or a servant.
Gives the sound bǔ, related to pū but drifted apart over time.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 这位贵族雇了好几个仆人。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi guìzú gùle hǎo jǐ gè púrén.
example.english: This nobleman employed several servants.
example.fact: In Victorian-era Britain, a single large aristocratic household could employ dozens of servants, from butlers and footmen to scullery maids, each with strictly defined duties and a place in a rigid internal hierarchy. Historians estimate that by the late 1800s, domestic service was the single largest employment category for working-class women in England.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 滑 describes something as slick or slippery, like a wet surface.
骨 (gǔ) is only distantly related in sound to huá — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.
禾 (grain) — 稽 was originally tied to inspecting or delaying, later meaning to examine.
旨 (zhǐ) gives a sound only distantly related to jī today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他的动作十分滑稽,把大家都逗笑了。
example.pinyin: tā de dòngzuò shífēn huájī, bǎ dàjiā dōu dòuxiàole.
example.english: His movements were very comical and made everyone laugh.
example.fact: Laughter triggers the release of endorphins in the brain and can measurably lower levels of stress hormones in the body, effects studied by researchers in a field sometimes called gelotology. Some hospitals have used this research to justify formal 'laughter therapy' programs aimed at reducing pain and anxiety in patients.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 怎's meaning 'how' relates to a mental inquiry, what's on one's mind.
乍 (zhà) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from zěn.

么 derives from 幺, a pictograph of a small twisted skein of silk thread, symbolizing something tiny or insignificant. As a standalone character it was later borrowed purely for its sound, becoming the light, toneless question particle seen in words like 什么 and 怎么.
着 is a variant of 著; its top element 艹 (grass, plant) combined with 者 originally referred to garments woven from plant fiber.
From 'to wear, to attach' the character broadened into its many modern uses — as a durative particle, and in words like 着火 ('to catch fire') and 着急 ('to worry').

example.hanzi: 这事儿你打算怎么着?
example.pinyin: zhè shìr nǐ dǎsuàn zěnmezhāo?
example.english: What are you going to do about this matter?
example.fact: A widely cited study from the University of Michigan found that young children ask several hundred questions a day on average during their peak years of curiosity, far more than most adults realize. Researchers see this relentless questioning as a key driver of early cognitive development, helping children build working models of how the world operates.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 漫 describes water overflowing and spreading everywhere.
曼 (màn) gives the sound — an exact match with 漫.
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.

example.hanzi: 这是一段漫长而艰难的旅程。
example.pinyin: zhè shì yī duàn màncháng ér jiānnán de lǚchéng.
example.english: This was a long and difficult journey.
example.fact: Light from the Andromeda Galaxy, the nearest large galaxy to our own, takes about 2.5 million years to reach Earth, meaning the light arriving tonight left long before modern humans existed. Despite that immense distance, Andromeda is on a slow collision course with the Milky Way, with the two galaxies expected to merge in roughly four billion years.
